Job 23:15#0 Ἀ. Θ..unitText: Ο΄. διὰ τοῦτο ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἐσπούδακα, νουθετούμενος δὲ ἐφρόντισα αὐτοῦ.^13 ※ Ἀ. Θ. ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ· κατανοήσω, καὶ πτοηθήσομαι ἐξ αὐτοῦ.^14

variants.reading: ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ· κατανοήσω, καὶ πτοηθήσομαι ἐξ αὐτοῦ.^14
variants.n: Künftige Bestürzung und Furcht statt vergangener Eile und Sorge.
variants.en: Future alarm and fear rather than past haste and concern.

0056.0.13.la: In hodiernis τῶν Ο΄ exemplaribus haec, διὰ τοῦτο—ἐφρόντισα αὐτοῦ, pro v. 14 habentur, etsi Hebraeis prorsus dissimilia: deinde illa, ἐπὶ τούτῳ—ἐξ αὐτοῦ, pro versione LXXvirali v. 15 venditantur. Alii vero cum Grabio rectius statuerunt, v. 14, qui Latine sonat: _Nam perficiet statutum meum_ (id quod in me statuit), _et talia multa_ sunt _cum eo_, tam in versione LXXvirali, quam in ceterorum interpretum reliquiis prorsus desiderari; quaeque hodie in editis leguntur pro duplici interpretatione v. 15 habenda esse.
0056.0.13.en: In the present-day copies τῶν Ο΄ these words, διὰ τοῦτο—ἐφρόντισα αὐτοῦ, are taken for v. 14, although entirely unlike the Hebrew: then those words, ἐπὶ τούτῳ—ἐξ αὐτοῦ, are passed off as the Septuagint version of v. 15. Others, however, with Grabe, have more correctly determined that v. 14, which in Latin runs: “_For he will perform my appointed portion_ (that which he has appointed for me), _and many such things_ are _with him_,” is entirely wanting both in the Septuagint version and in the remains of the other interpreters; and that what is read today in the printed editions should be taken as a double rendering of v. 15.

0056.0.14.la: “Colbertinus, praemisso asterisco, Ἐκ τῶν Ἀκύλα καὶ Θ. οἱ β΄. τετάραγμαι. Illud autem τετάραγμαι videtur item esse Aquilae et Theodotionis, loco τοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ, quod hodie in versione τῶν Ο΄ legitur. Ed. Lat. Hieron. habet _turbabor_, et hos duos versic. asterisco notat.”—_Montef._ Syro-hex. in textu affert: ※ Θ. (non Ἀ. Θ.) ἐν τούτῳ (ܒܗܕܐ) ἀπὸ πρ. αὐτοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ (ܐܬܬܪܗܒ[?]) κ. τ. ἑ. Cum vero κατασπουδασθῶ Aquilam prorsus referat (vid. Hex. ad 2 Reg. iv. 1. Psal. ii. 5. vi. 3, 10), magis credibile est, τετάραγμαι ad alium interpretem pertinere. Vid. not. seq.
0056.0.14.en: “The Colbertine, with an asterisk prefixed, Ἐκ τῶν Ἀκύλα καὶ Θ. οἱ β΄. τετάραγμαι. That τετάραγμαι seems likewise to be Aquila's and Theodotion's, in place τοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ, which is read today in the version τῶν Ο΄. The Latin Ed. of Jerome has _I shall be troubled_, and marks these two versicles with an asterisk.”—_Montef._ Syro-hex. in the text gives: ※ Θ. (not Ἀ. Θ.) ἐν τούτῳ (ܒܗܕܐ) ἀπὸ πρ. αὐτοῦ κατασπουδασθῶ (ܐܬܬܪܗܒ[?]) κ. τ. ἑ. But since κατασπουδασθῶ entirely recalls Aquila (see Hex. on 2 Reg. iv. 1. Psal. ii. 5. vi. 3, 10), it is more credible that τετάραγμαι belongs to another interpreter. See the next note.

Job 23:15#1 Ἀ..unitText: Ο΄. ἐσπούδακα. Ἀ. κατασπουδασθῶ. Σ. τετάραγμαι.^15

variants.n: Eine künftig erlittene Bestürzung statt bereits vollzogener Eile.
variants.en: Future alarm suffered rather than haste already undertaken.

0056.0.15.la: “Syro-hex. ܣ. ܡܫܓܫ ܐܢܐ ܀ Σ. ταράσσω. Syriac. verbum vitiose scriptum videtur; offendit enim activa forma participii.”—_Middeld._ Defendi quidem potest ܡܫܓܫ ܐܢܐ, sensu intransitivo, _tumultuabor_, θορυβήσω (cf. Hex. ad Psal. ii. 1. lviii. 15). Quoniam vero in cod. diserte scriptum esse ܡܫܓܫ[?] ܐܢܐ certior factus sum, non dubitavi lectionem anonymam τετάραγμαι Symmacho vindicare. Praeterea notandum est, Nobilium ad ἐσπούδακα afferre: Schol. ἐθροήθην καὶ ἐταράχθην (Cod. 248 in marg. addit: ἀγνοῶν τῆς πληγῆς τὴν αἰτίαν); necnon ad illa, κατασπουδασθῶ, κατανοήσω: Schol. ἀμηχανῶ καὶ κατανοῶν πτοοῦμαι, quod et Cod. 248 in marg. habet.
0056.0.15.en: “Syro-hex. ܣ. ܡܫܓܫ ܐܢܐ ܀ Σ. ταράσσω. The Syriac verb seems to be wrongly written; for the active form of the participle is offensive.”—_Middeld._ ܡܫܓܫ ܐܢܐ can indeed be defended, in an intransitive sense, _I shall be in tumult_, θορυβήσω (cf. Hex. on Psal. ii. 1. lviii. 15). But since I have been assured that in the codex ܡܫܓܫ[?] ܐܢܐ is expressly written, I have not hesitated to claim the anonymous reading τετάραγμαι for Symmachus. Moreover it should be noted that Nobilius gives on ἐσπούδακα: Schol. ἐθροήθην καὶ ἐταράχθην (Cod. 248 in the margin adds: ἀγνοῶν τῆς πληγῆς τὴν αἰτίαν); and also on the words κατασπουδασθῶ, κατανοήσω: Schol. ἀμηχανῶ καὶ κατανοῶν πτοοῦμαι, which Cod. 248 also has in the margin.

0058.0.25.la: Syro-hex. ܐ. ܠܐ ܢܨܛܠܐ ܠܐܘܪܚܐ ܠܐ ܡܬܕܪܟܢܝܬܐ ܕܟܪ̈ܡܐ. ܘܠܚܡܝܡܘܬܐ ܢܒܙܘܢ ܡܛܠܨܢܐܝܬ[?] ܀ ܣ. ܠܐ ܢܗܦܘܟ ܠܐܘܪܚܐ ܕܟܪ̈ܡܐ ܒܨܗܝܐ. ܐܦ ܚܘܡܐ ܒܙܘ ܀ ܬ. ܠܐ ܢܨܛܠܐ ܠܐܘܪܚܐ ܕܟܪ̈ܡܐ ܒܨܗܝܐ. ܐܦ ܓܝܪ ܗܢܘܢ ܡܫܠܚܝܢ ܀ Insigne fragmentum, de quo Montef. οὐδὲ γρύ. Middeldorpfii annotatio haec est: “Ἀ. οὐκ ἐκκλινεῖ εἰς ὁδὸν ἀνεπίβατον (Mal. i. 3) τῶν ἀμπελώνων, καὶ εἰς θέρμην (Job. vi. 17. Psal. xviii. 7) ἐκβιάσονται (Prov. xvi. 26). Σ. οὐκ ἀναστρέψει εἰς ὁδὸν τῶν ἀμπελώνων διψώδη, καὶ καῦμα ἁρπάζουσι. Θ. οὐκ ἐκκλινεῖ εἰς ὁδὸν τῶν ἀμπελώνων ἐν δίψῃ (Psal. ciii. 12. cvi. 33. Jesai. xli. 17), καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ συλῶσι.” Graeca Aquilae et Theodotionis non muto. Apud Sym. scribendum esse ἥρπασαν s. διήρπασαν pro ἁρπάζουσι quivis videt. Porro διψώδης sonaret ܨܗܝܬܐ (Psal. cvi. 9. Jesai. xxxv. 6) vel ܨܗܝܢܐ[?] (Prov. ix. 12). Quod hic legitur ܒܨܗܝܐ non potest esse nisi infinitivus, τοῦ διψᾶν s. διψῆσαι.

Middeldorpf's annotation is this: “Ἀ. οὐκ ἐκκλινεῖ εἰς ὁδὸν ἀνεπίβατον (Mal. i. 3) τῶν ἀμπελώνων, καὶ εἰς θέρμην (Job. vi. 17. Psal. xviii. 7) ἐκβιάσονται (Prov. xvi. 26). Jesai. xli. 17), καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ συλῶσι.” I do not change the Greek of Aquila and Theodotion. In Sym. anyone can see that ἥρπασαν or διήρπασαν should be written for ἁρπάζουσι. Further, διψώδης would be ܨܗܝܬܐ (Psal. cvi. 9. Jesai. xxxv. 6) or ܨܗܝܢܐ[?] (Prov. ix. 12). What is read here, ܒܨܗܝܐ, can be nothing but an infinitive, τοῦ διψᾶν or διψῆσαι.

Nam versio illa Symmachi ad sequentem vocem pertinet, ut in iisdem MSS. indicatur, et res ipsa docet.” Scilicet Nicetas testatur: ἀντὶ δὲ τοῦ θῖνας, Θ. μὲν ὀχυρώματα, Σ. δὲ ῥεῖθρα ἐξέδωκαν. Job 29:2#0 Ἀ. Σ..unitText: Ο΄. τίς ἄν με θείη κατὰ μῆνα ἔμπροσθεν ἡμερῶν ὧν με ὁ θεὸς ἐφύλαξεν; Ἀ. Σ. τίς δῴη με κατὰ τοὺς μῆνας τοὺς πρώτους, κατὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἃς ὁ θεὸς ἐφύλασσέ με.^1

variants.reading: τίς δῴη με κατὰ τοὺς μῆνας τοὺς πρώτους, κατὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἃς ὁ θεὸς ἐφύλασσέ με.^1
variants.n: Mehrere frühere Monate statt eines Monats vor den bewahrten Tagen.
variants.en: Several former months rather than one month preceding the protected days.

0063.1.1.la: Sic Julian. apud Nicet. Colb. et Reg. unus priorem versiculum Aquilae et Symmacho, posteriorem Theodotioni tribuunt.
0063.1.1.en: Thus Julian in Nicet. Colb. and one Reg. ascribe the first versicle to Aquila and Symmachus, the second to Theodotion.

Job 29:3#0 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. ὡς ὅτε ηὔγει. Σ. ἔλαμπεν.^2

variants.n: Ein anderes Verb bedeutet ebenfalls „er leuchtete“.
variants.en: Another verb likewise means “it shone.”

0063.1.2.la: Cod. 139. Montef. ex Colb. et Reg. affert: Ἄλλος· ἔλαμπεν.
0063.1.2.en: Cod. 139. Montef. gives from Colb. and Reg.: Ἄλλος· ἔλαμπεν.

Job 29:4#0 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. ὅτε ἤμην ἐπιβρίθων ὁδούς.^3 Σ. ὥσπερ ἤμην ἐν ἡμέραις νεότητός μου.^4

variants.reading: ὥσπερ ἤμην ἐν ἡμέραις νεότητός μου.^4
variants.n: Jugendtage statt des Beschwerens von Wegen.
variants.en: Days of youth rather than weighing down roads.

0063.1.3.la: Syro-hex. ὁδοῖς habet, cum scholio: “Justitia scilicet et abundantia opum (ܙܕܝܩܘܬܐ ܥܡ ܡܘܬܪܘܬܐ ܕܥܘܬܪ̈ܐ ܀).”
0063.1.3.en: Syro-hex. has ὁδοῖς, with the scholium: “Namely justice and abundance of riches (ܙܕܝܩܘܬܐ ܥܡ ܡܘܬܪܘܬܐ ܕܥܘܬܪ̈ܐ ܀).”

0063.1.4.la: Olymp. et “omnes.” Colb. et Reg. unus habent: ὥσπερ ὅτε ἤμην.
0063.1.4.en: Olymp. and “all.” Colb. and one Reg. have: ὥσπερ ὅτε ἤμην.

Job 29:4#1 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. ὅτε ὁ θεὸς ἐπισκοπὴν ἐποιεῖτο τοῦ οἴκου μου. Σ. ὁπότε περιέφρασσεν ὁ θεὸς τὴν σκηνήν μου.^5

variants.reading: ὁπότε περιέφρασσεν ὁ θεὸς τὴν σκηνήν μου.^5
variants.n: Gott umzäunte sein Zelt statt sein Haus zu besuchen.
variants.en: God enclosed his tent rather than visiting his house.

0063.1.5.la: Olymp. et “omnes.” Drusius ex Nobil. κύριος pro θεὸς habet.
0063.1.5.en: Olymp. and “all.” Drusius, from Nobil., has κύριος for θεὸς.

Job 29:5#0 Ἄλλος.unitText: Ο΄. κύκλῳ δέ μου οἱ παῖδες. [Ἄλλος· ἀγόμενοι ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ.]^6

variants.n: „Von mir geführt“ statt „um mich“.
variants.en: “Led by me” rather than “around me.”

0063.1.6.la: Colb. et Reg. unus. Est scholium ex Olymp., cujus verba sunt: τοὺς δὲ παῖδας κατὰ θεῖον ἐκτρέφων βούλημα, ἀγομένους ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ κ. τ. ἑ.
0063.1.6.en: Colb. and one Reg. It is a scholium from Olymp., whose words are: τοὺς δὲ παῖδας κατὰ θεῖον ἐκτρέφων βούλημα, ἀγομένους ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ κ. τ. ἑ.

variants.n: Ein anderes Wort bezeichnet ebenfalls junge Menschen.
variants.en: Another word likewise denotes young people.

0063.1.7.la: Reg. unus. Colb. autem deficit usque ad Cap. xxxi.
0063.1.7.en: One Reg. Colb., however, fails as far as Cap. xxxi.

variants.n: „Sie standen bereit“ statt „alle standen“.
variants.en: “They stood by” rather than “all stood.”

0063.1.8.la: Reg. unus, pro קָמוּ an pro עָמָדוּ incertum.
0063.1.8.en: One Reg.; whether for קָמוּ or for עָמָדוּ is uncertain.

Job 29:9#0 Οἱ λοιποί.unitText: Ο΄. ἁδροὶ δέ. Οἱ λοιποί· οἱ ἄρχοντες.^9

variants.n: „Die Herrscher“ statt „die Wohlhabenden“.
variants.en: “The rulers” rather than “the prosperous.”

Job 29:11#0 Ἀ. Σ..unitText: Ο΄. ἐξέκλινε. Ἀ. Σ. ἐμαρτύρησε περὶ ἐμοῦ.^11

variants.n: „Es zeugte über mich“ statt „es wandte sich ab“.
variants.en: “It testified concerning me” rather than “it turned aside.”

variants.n: Der Wunsch nach dem Segen eines Vergehenden wird ergänzt.
variants.en: The wish for the blessing of one perishing is added.

0063.1.12.la: Sic Syro-hex. et sub aster. Hieron.
0063.1.12.en: Thus Syro-hex. and under the asterisk Jerome.

0063.1.13.la: Syro-hex. ܣ. ܒܘܪܟܬܗ ܕܐܒܝܕܐ ܥܠܝ ܐܬܝܐ ܗܘܬ ܀ Montef. ex Nicet., Orat. et Regiis affert tantummodo: Σ. κατήντα.
0063.1.13.en: Syro-hex. ܣ. ܒܘܪܟܬܗ ܕܐܒܝܕܐ ܥܠܝ ܐܬܝܐ ܗܘܬ ܀ Montef. gives from Nicet., Orat. and the Regii only: Σ. κατήντα.

Job 29:13#0 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. Vacabat. ※ Ἀ. Θ. εὐλογία ἀπολλυμένου ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἔλθοι.^12 Σ. εὐλογία ἀπολλυμένου ἐπ’ ἐμὲ κατήντα.^13

variants.n: Der empfangene Segen eines Vergehenden wird ergänzt.
variants.en: The received blessing of one perishing is added.

0063.1.12.en: Thus Syro-hex. and under the asterisk Jerome.

Job 29:13#1 Θ..unitText: Ο΄. στόμα δὲ χήρας με εὐλόγησε. Θ. καὶ καρδίαν χήρας ηὔφρανα.^14

variants.n: Er erfreut das Witwenherz, statt dass ihr Mund ihn segnet.
variants.en: He gladdens the widow’s heart rather than her mouth blessing him.

0063.1.14.la: Olymp., Orat. et Regii. Eadem habet Cod. 250 in marg. sine nomine. H 2
0063.1.14.en: Olymp., Orat. and the Regii. Cod. 250 has the same in the margin without a name.

Job 29:18#0 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. εἶπα δὲ, ἡ ἡλικία μου γηράσει. Σ. ἔλεγον δὲ μετὰ τῆς νοσσιᾶς μου γηράσειν.^15

variants.reading: ἔλεγον δὲ μετὰ τῆς νοσσιᾶς μου γηράσειν.^15
variants.n: Mit seiner Brut alt werden statt des allgemeinen Alterns.
variants.en: Growing old with his brood rather than aging generally.

Job 29:19#0 Θ..unitText: Ο΄. Vacabat. ※ Θ. ἡ ῥίζα —— ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ πορεύεται.^16

variants.reading: ἡ ῥίζα —— ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ πορεύεται.^16
variants.n: Der Abschnitt über bewässerte Wurzeln, Ehre und erneuerte Kraft wird ergänzt.
variants.en: The passage about watered roots, honour and renewed strength is added.

0064.0.16.la: Sic Syro-hex. Montef. asteriscum tantum praemittit, ut Hieron. et Cod. 248.
0064.0.16.en: Thus Syro-hex. Montef. prefixes only an asterisk, as do Hieron. and Cod. 248.

variants.n: „Sie lobten“ statt „sie achteten darauf“.
variants.en: “They praised” rather than “they paid attention.”

0064.0.18.la: Reg. unus. In fronte versiculi Codd. Alex. et 249 addunt πρεσβύτεροι, et sic Syro-hex. in marg.
0064.0.18.en: One Reg. At the beginning of the verse Codd. Alex. and 249 add πρεσβύτεροι, and so Syro-hex. in the margin.

Job 29:24#0 Σ..unitText: Ο΄. ἐὰν γελάσω πρὸς αὐτοὺς, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσωσι. Σ. προσεγέλων αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ οὐκ ἐπίστευον.^19

variants.reading: προσεγέλων αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ οὐκ ἐπίστευον.^19
variants.n: Wiederholtes vergangenes Lächeln statt einer zukünftigen Bedingung.
variants.en: Repeated past smiling rather than a future condition.

Job 29:24#1 Θ..unitText: Ο΄. Vacabat. ※ Θ. καὶ φῶς τοῦ προσώπου μου —— παρακαλῶν.^20

variants.reading: καὶ φῶς τοῦ προσώπου μου —— παρακαλῶν.^20
variants.n: Der Abschnitt vom leuchtenden Angesicht bis zum Trösten wird ergänzt.
variants.en: The passage from the radiant face to consolation is added.

0064.0.20.la: Sic sub ※ Θ. Syro-hex. Sub simplici aster. Montef., ut Hieron. et Cod. 248. Parsons. ad haec, καὶ φῶς κ.τ.ἑ.: “Θ. ἡ δόξα τῆς διδασκαλίας μου. Sic Cod. 139, et sine nom. Codd. 137, 138.” Scholium esse quivis videt.
0064.0.20.en: Thus under ※ Θ. Syro-hex. Under a simple asterisk Montef., as do Hieron. and Cod. 248. Parsons on these words, καὶ φῶς κ.τ.ἑ.: “Θ. ἡ δόξα τῆς διδασκαλίας μου. Thus Cod. 139, and without name Codd. 137, 138.” Anyone can see that it is a scholium.

0065.0.8.en: Syro-hex. ܐ. ܕܡܩܦܩܦܝܢ[?] ܡܫܚܐ ܥܠ ܢܨܒܬܐ. (In the passage Ezech. xvii. 22 Aquila rendered אֶקְטֹף by περικλάσω according to Codd. 86, 88.)

0065.0.9.en: Olymp., Orat., two Regii. Hieron.: ※ “_who gnawed the bark of trees._” The Syrian by mistake continues Aquila: ܟܕ ܦܫܚܝܢ[?] ܩܠܦ̈ܐ[?] ܕܐܝܠܢ̈ܐ ◆

0066.0.33.la: Montef. edidit: לְתַנִּים (v. 29). Ο΄. σειρήνων. Σ. ἀθυμῶν. Idem notat: “Reg. unus. Videtur autem esse vox corrupta. Forte αἰθυιῶν, _mergorum_ vel _fulicarum._” Schleusner. (qui ἀθύμων, invito codice, scribit) in _Nov. Thes._ s. v. ἄθυμος, ad בֹּכִים (v. 31) referendum esse putat. Semlero videbatur esse ipsum nomen Hebr. תַּנִּים Graece scriptum. Miror neminem conjecisse, Symmachum hac voce Hebraicum בְּלֹא חֵמָה (Comp. ἄνευ θυμοῦ, Pesch. ܕܠܐ ܚܡܬܐ[?]) exprimere voluisse.
0066.0.33.en: Montef. edited: לְתַנִּים (v. 29). Ο΄. σειρήνων. Σ. ἀθυμῶν. He also notes: “One Reg. But it seems to be a corrupt word. Perhaps αἰθυιῶν, _of divers_ or _of coots._” Schleusner (who writes ἀθύμων, against the MS.) in _Nov. Thes._ s. v. ἄθυμος thinks it is to be referred to בֹּכִים (v. 31). To Semler it seemed to be the Hebrew noun תַּנִּים itself written in Greek. I am surprised that no one has conjectured that Symmachus meant by this word to express the Hebrew בְּלֹא חֵמָה (Comp. ἄνευ θυμοῦ, Pesch. ܕܠܐ ܚܡܬܐ[?]).

0069.1.13.la: Olymp.: Ἕτερα ἀντίγραφα μετὰ τὸ, ἐρῶ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων, ἔχει καὶ τούτους τοὺς στίχους· ἰδοὺ ἤκουσα τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἠνωτισάμην ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν. Sic Codd. III, 23, nisi quod ἐνωτισάμην μέχρι σ. ὑ. in utroque legitur, et ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἤκουσα in Cod. 23.
0069.1.13.en: Olymp.: Ἕτερα ἀντίγραφα μετὰ τὸ, ἐρῶ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων, ἔχει καὶ τούτους τοὺς στίχους· ἰδοὺ ἤκουσα τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἠνωτισάμην ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν. Thus Codd. III, 23, except that ἐνωτισάμην μέχρι σ. ὑ. is read in both, and ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἤκουσα in Cod. 23.

0069.1.16.la: Haec vulgo τοῖς Ο΄ tribuuntur; sed Syro-hex. inde ab ἄχρις οὗ ad finem v. 12 ἐξ ὑμῶν omnia Theodotioni vindicat. Idem ἐρῶ γὰρ om. in textu, sed in marg. habet: ἐρῶ γάρ. “Scholium (ܣܟܘܠܝܘܢ). In multis exemplaribus (ܣ̈ܓܝܐܐ) ante ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων positum est ἀναγγελῶ (ܡܘܕܥ[?] ܐܢܐ) γάρ. Non positum erat in Tetraplis (ܒܐܪ̈ܒܥܐ[?] ܦܐ̈ܬܐ[?]).” Lectio ἀναγγελῶ γὰρ reperitur in Cod. 55.
0069.1.16.en: These are commonly assigned τοῖς Ο΄; but Syro-hex. claims for Theodotion everything from ἄχρις οὗ to the end of v. 12 ἐξ ὑμῶν. The same omits ἐρῶ γὰρ in the text, but has in the margin: ἐρῶ γάρ. “Scholium (ܣܟܘܠܝܘܢ). In many copies (ܣ̈ܓܝܐܐ) before ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων there is placed ἀναγγελῶ (ܡܘܕܥ[?] ܐܢܐ) γάρ. It was not placed in the Tetrapla (ܒܐܪ̈ܒܥܐ[?] ܦܐ̈ܬܐ[?]).” The reading ἀναγγελῶ γὰρ is found in Cod. 55.

0069.1.17.la: Colb., Reg. unus. Olymp. mendose affert: ἠκροασάμην ἐφ’ ὅσον ἐξητάσητε λόγους κ. τ. ἑ. Symmachum vertisse videtur Hieron., omisso in fine ἐνενόουν: ※ _et audivi vestram prudentiam, usquequo discuteretis sermones, et donec intelligerem vos._
0069.1.17.en: Colb., one Reg. Olymp. cites faultily: ἠκροασάμην ἐφ’ ὅσον ἐξητάσητε λόγους κ. τ. ἑ. Hieron. seems to have translated Symmachus, omitting at the end

variants.en: The passage about waiting for word examination and the lack of refutation is added.

0070.0.19.la: Colb.: ※ Ἐκ Θ. οἱ δ΄. Montef. vero hos quatuor versiculos a καὶ μέχρι ὑμῶν incipit, et usque ad προσθέμενοι (v. 13) continuat, invito, quem nos secuti sumus, Syro.
0070.0.19.en: Colb.: ※ Ἐκ Θ. οἱ δ΄. But Montef. begins these four lines with καὶ μέχρι ὑμῶν, and continues them as far as προσθέμενοι (v. 13), against the Syrian, whom we have followed.

0070.0.21.la: Nobile fragmentum interpretis nescio cujus ex margine Syro-hex., ut in apographo Norberg. exstat, versiculis tantum distinctis, exscribam. [Huic fragmento in codice, cum indice ad κυρίῳ προσθέμενοι lectorem referente, praemissa sunt verba, ܕܠܐ ܦܩܚ̈ܢ[?] ◆, h. e. _absona_, quod de versione textuali praedicari videtur. In marg. autem inferiori cum eodem indice appositum est scholium: “In Tetraplis quidem legebatur ut in margine (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܒܪ); in exemplari vero Eusebii et Pamphili, ut in textu (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܓܘ).”] ※ ܫܠܝܛܐ ܐܚܕ ܠܗ ܘܠܘ ܓܒܪܐ. ※ ܘܠܐ ܣܡ[?] ܠܘܬܝ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܘܒܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܟܘܢ ܠܐ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܠܗ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܐܬܬܥܝܪܘ[?] ܡܢܗܘܢ ܡܡܠܠ̈ܐ. ※ ܘܣܟܝܬ ܡܛܠ ܕܠܐ ܡܠܠܬ. ※ ܡܛܠ ܕܩܡܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ ܡܢܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ. ※ ܡܚܘܐ ܐܢܐ ܝܕܥܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ↙. ܟܒܪ[?] ܕܡܠܐ[?] ܓܝܪ ܐܢܐ ܡܢ ܡ̈ܠܐ. ܠܡܐܡܪ ܗܠܝܢ ◆ Middeldorpfius haec Graece quidem exprimere non ausus est: Latina ejus, male divisa et Syriacis parum accommodata, subjungam tamen. ※ _Tyrannus occupavit illum, non homo. Neque mihi verba opposuit; verbis vestris non obstitissem illi. Sermone improbo usi sunt. Responsum iterum iis abreptum. Exspectavi ita ut nihil dicerem, propterea quod adstabant; jam non amplius oppositionem faciunt. Et ego partes meas suscipiam, proferam et ego sententiam meam↙. Nam verborum plenus jam ea sum prolaturus._ Tantum addidit: “De auctore hujus interpretationis nil definiri potest.” Mirum profecto Criticum optimum non animadvertisse, Syriaca sua cum Latinis Hieronymi a Montef. allatis ad verbum fere convenire. Haec autem sunt: ※ _Dominus abjecit eum, et non vir._ ※ _Necdum ad me locutus est:_ ※ _et in sermonibus vestris non respondebo ei._ ※ _Obstupuerunt, non responderunt ultra:_ ※ _defecerunt ab eis sermones._ ※ _Quia ergo exspectavi, et non sunt loquuti,_ ※ _et steterunt, et non responderunt ultra:_ ※ _respondebo et ego partem meam,_ ※ _et annuntiabo scientiam meam._ In versiculo primo Hebr. אֵל Syriace est ܫܠܝܛܐ, Graece ὁ ἰσχυρὸς, quod tralatitium est. Sed offendit verbum ܐܚܕ, _apprehendit_, quod neque Hebraeo נָדַף, _fugavit_, neque Hieronymiano _abjecit_ commode aptari potest. Tentabam ܐܫܕܝ[?], quod Syrus noster pro ἀπέρριψε posuit Psal. l. 13. lxx. 9, et saepius, nisi hoc ab ܐܚܕ nimis remotum videretur. Ergo in medio relinquo. [Tardius certior factus sum, in codice scriptum exstare ܢܫܕܐ[?], ἀπορρίψει.] Transeamus ad v. 4, ubi Middeld. jungens ܕܒܘܠܐ cum praecedenti ܡܩܒܠܬܐ, de _sermone improbo_ intellexit. Hebraica sunt, חַתּוּ לֹא עָנוּ עוֹד, quae luculenter expressit Hieron.: _obstupuerunt, non responderunt ultra;_ nec deterius Theodotio: ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι. Quid multa? Pro Syriacis ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ fidenter corrigo ܬܘܗܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ [sic in cod.], ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἐποιοῦντο. Ponitur ܬܘܗ pro ἐπτοήθη Job. xi. 16. xxiii. 15. Jesai. xxxi. 4, etc. Quae autem post cuneolum leguntur, quaeque divinando vertit Middeld.: _nam verborum plenus jam ea sum prolaturus_ (!), non sunt nisi scholium Syri interpretis: “_Ad illud,_ πλήρης γάρ εἰμι ῥημάτων (v. 18), _junge haec._” Restat quaestio, cuinam potissimum trium interpretum insigne hoc fragmentum tribuendum sit. Theodotionis esse non potest, quia hic, testibus Colbert. et Syro, post ἐπτοήθησαν pergit: οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι· ἐπαλαίωσαν ἐξ αὐτῶν λόγους κ.τ.ἑ. quae hodie in versione LXXvirali leguntur. Versio tam scrupulosa est, ut Aquilae vindicari possit, si excipias locutionem ἀπόκρισιν ποιεῖσθαι pro עָנָה, quam vix admiserit istius interpretis usus. Superest igitur Symmachus, cui particulam τὸ μέρος μου diserte tribuit Colbertinus, quemque in vertendis vv. 11, 12 sectatus esse videtur Hieron.
0070.0.21.en: A remarkable fragment of some unknown translator from the margin of Syro-hex., as it stands in Norberg's transcript, I shall copy out, only distinguishing the lines. [To this fragment in the MS., with a sign referring the reader to κυρίῳ προσθέμενοι, are prefixed the words ܕܠܐ ܦܩܚ̈ܢ[?] ◆, i.e. _incongruous_, which seems to be said of the textual version. But in the lower margin, with the same sign, a scholium is added: “In the Tetrapla it was read as in the margin (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܒܪ); but in the copy of Eusebius and Pamphilus, as in the text (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܓܘ).”] ※ ܫܠܝܛܐ ܐܚܕ ܠܗ ܘܠܘ ܓܒܪܐ. ※ ܘܠܐ ܣܡ[?] ܠܘܬܝ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܘܒܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܟܘܢ ܠܐ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܠܗ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܐܬܬܥܝܪܘ[?] ܡܢܗܘܢ ܡܡܠܠ̈ܐ. ※ ܘܣܟܝܬ ܡܛܠ ܕܠܐ ܡܠܠܬ. ※ ܡܛܠ ܕܩܡܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ ܡܢܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ. ※ ܡܚܘܐ ܐܢܐ ܝܕܥܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ↙. ܟܒܪ[?] ܕܡܠܐ[?] ܓܝܪ ܐܢܐ ܡܢ ܡ̈ܠܐ. ܠܡܐܡܪ ܗܠܝܢ ◆ Middeldorpf did not venture to express these in Greek; I shall nevertheless append his Latin, badly divided and ill suited to the Syriac. ※ “_A tyrant seized him, not a man. Nor did he set words against me; to your words I would not have opposed him. They used wicked speech. The answer was again snatched from them. I waited so as to say nothing, because they stood by; now they no longer make opposition. I too will take up my part, I too will bring forth my opinion↙. For being full of words I am now about to bring them forth._” He added only: “Concerning the author of this interpretation nothing can be determined.” It is truly surprising that this excellent critic did not notice that his Syriac agrees almost word for word with the Latin of Hieronymus cited by Montef. This is as follows: ※ “_The Lord cast him off, and not man._” ※ “_He has not yet spoken to me:_” ※ “_and in your speeches I will not answer him._” ※ “_They were astonished, they answered no more:_” ※ “_words failed them._” ※ “_Since then I waited, and they did not speak,_” ※ “_and they stood, and answered no more:_” ※ “_I too will answer my part,_” ※ “_and will declare my knowledge._” In the first line the Hebrew אֵל is in Syriac ܫܠܝܛܐ, in Greek ὁ ἰσχυρὸς, which is customary. But the verb ܐܚܕ, _seized_, gives offence, since it cannot fitly be adapted either to the Hebrew נָדַף, _drove away_, or to Hieronymus' _cast off_. I tried ܐܫܕܝ[?], which our Syrian put for ἀπέρριψε Psal. l. 13. lxx. 9, and frequently, were it not that this seems too remote from ܐܚܕ. Therefore I leave it undecided. [Later I was informed that in the MS. ܢܫܕܐ[?], ἀπορρίψει, stands written.] Let us pass to v. 4, where Middeld., joining ܕܒܘܠܐ with the preceding ܡܩܒܠܬܐ, understood it of _wicked speech_. The Hebrew is חַתּוּ לֹא עָנוּ עוֹד, which Hieron. expressed clearly: “_they were astonished, they answered no more;_” nor less well Theodotion: ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι. In short, for the Syriac ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ I confidently correct ܬܘܗܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ [thus in the MS.], ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἐποιοῦντο. ܬܘܗ is used for ἐπτοήθη Job. xi. 16. xxiii. 15. But in the lower margin, with the same sign, a scholium is added: “In the Tetrapla it was read as in the margin (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܒܪ); but in the copy of Eusebius and Pamphilus, as in the text (ܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܠܓܘ).”] ※ ܫܠܝܛܐ ܐܚܕ ܠܗ ܘܠܘ ܓܒܪܐ. ※ ܘܠܐ ܣܡ[?] ܠܘܬܝ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܘܒܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܟܘܢ ܠܐ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܠܗ ܡܩܒܠܬܐ[?]. ※ ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܐܬܬܥܝܪܘ[?] ܡܢܗܘܢ ܡܡܠܠ̈ܐ. ※ ܘܣܟܝܬ ܡܛܠ ܕܠܐ ܡܠܠܬ. ※ ܡܛܠ ܕܩܡܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܘ ܦܘܢܝ ܡܠܬܐ ܬܘܒ. ※ ܡܦܢܐ ܐܢܐ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ ܡܢܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ. ※ ܡܚܘܐ ܐܢܐ ܝܕܥܬܐ ܕܝܠܝ ܐܦ ܐܢܐ↙. ܟܒܪ[?] ܕܡܠܐ[?] ܓܝܪ ܐܢܐ ܡܢ ܡ̈ܠܐ. ܠܡܐܡܪ ܗܠܝܢ ◆ Middeldorpf did not venture to express these in Greek; I shall nevertheless append his Latin, badly divided and ill suited to the Syriac. ※ “_A tyrant seized him, not a man. Nor did he set words against me; to your words I would not have opposed him. They used wicked speech. The answer was again snatched from them. I waited so as to say nothing, because they stood by; now they no longer make opposition. I too will take up my part, I too will bring forth my opinion↙. For being full of words I am now about to bring them forth._” He added only: “Concerning the author of this interpretation nothing can be determined.” It is truly surprising that this excellent critic did not notice that his Syriac agrees almost word for word with the Latin of Hieronymus cited by Montef. This is as follows: ※ “_The Lord cast him off, and not man._” ※ “_He has not yet spoken to me:_” ※ “_and in your speeches I will not answer him._” ※ “_They were astonished, they answered no more:_” ※ “_words failed them._” ※ “_Since then I waited, and they did not speak,_” ※ “_and they stood, and answered no more:_” ※ “_I too will answer my part,_” ※ “_and will declare my knowledge._” In the first line the Hebrew אֵל is in Syriac ܫܠܝܛܐ, in Greek ὁ ἰσχυρὸς, which is customary. But the verb ܐܚܕ, _seized_, gives offence, since it cannot fitly be adapted either to the Hebrew נָדַף, _drove away_, or to Hieronymus' _cast off_. I tried ܐܫܕܝ[?], which our Syrian put for ἀπέρριψε Psal. l. 13. lxx. 9, and frequently, were it not that this seems too remote from ܐܚܕ. Therefore I leave it undecided. [Later I was informed that in the MS. ܢܫܕܐ[?], ἀπορρίψει, stands written.] Let us pass to v. 4, where Middeld., joining ܕܒܘܠܐ with the preceding ܡܩܒܠܬܐ, understood it of _wicked speech_. The Hebrew is חַתּוּ לֹא עָנוּ עוֹד, which Hieron. expressed clearly: “_they were astonished, they answered no more;_” nor less well Theodotion: ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι. In short, for the Syriac ܕܒܘܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ I confidently correct ܬܘܗܘ ܠܐ ܥܒܕܝܢ ܗܘܘ [thus in the MS.], ἐπτοήθησαν, οὐκ ἐποιοῦντο. ܬܘܗ is used for ἐπτοήθη Job. xi. 16. xxiii. 15. 0071.1.12.la: “Lectiones Aquilae et Symmachi sic omnes habent: ad Aquilam Drusius legit ἐκδικάσω, male.”—_Montef._ Ἐκδικάσω est error Nobilii. Aquilae Montef. tribuit πρὸς αὐτοὺς, sed αὐτὸν habent Olymp. et Syro-hex., cujus interpretatio haec est: ܐ. ܡܢܐ ܗܟܝܠ ܠܘܬܗ ܐܕܘܢ[?]. ܡܛܠ ܕܟܠܗܘܢ ܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܗ ܠܐ ܡܦܢܐ ◆ ܣ. ܡܛܠ ܗܢܐ ܕܠܘܬܗ ܕܐܢ ܐܢܬ. ܟܠܗܘܢ ܓܝܪ ܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܗ ܕܠܐ ܚܪܝܢܐ ◆ “Syriacum ܐܕܘܢ[?] proculdubio vitiosum est, ita ut legendum sit ܬܕܘܢ[?] [vel ܐܕܘܢ[?], si forte Syrus in apographo suo mendosum δικάσω s. ἐκδικάσω invenerit].”—_Middeld._ Reapse in cod. est ܐܕܘܢ[?]. Apud Symmachum pro τί interrogantis Syrus ὅτι s. διότι legisse videtur: Graecam autem locutionem αὐτῷ διαδικάζῃ ita vertit quasi esset πρὸς αὐτὸν δικάζῃ.
0071.1.12.en: “The readings of Aquila and Symmachus all have thus: for Aquila Drusius reads ἐκδικάσω, wrongly.”—_Montef._ Ἐκδικάσω is an error of Nobilius. Montef. assigns to Aquila πρὸς αὐτοὺς, but αὐτὸν is in Olymp. and Syro-hex., whose rendering is this: ܐ. ܡܢܐ ܗܟܝܠ ܠܘܬܗ ܐܕܘܢ[?]. ܡܛܠ ܕܟܠܗܘܢ ܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܗ ܠܐ ܡܦܢܐ ◆ ܣ. ܡܛܠ ܗܢܐ ܕܠܘܬܗ ܕܐܢ ܐܢܬ. ܟܠܗܘܢ ܓܝܪ ܡ̈ܠܐ ܕܝܠܗ ܕܠܐ ܚܪܝܢܐ ◆ “The Syriac ܐܕܘܢ[?] is without doubt faulty, so that ܬܕܘܢ[?] should be read [or ܐܕܘܢ[?], if perhaps the Syrian found in his copy the faulty δικάσω or ἐκδικάσω].”—_Middeld._ In fact the MS. has ܐܕܘܢ[?]. In Symmachus the Syrian seems to have read ὅτι or διότι for the interrogative τί: and he rendered the Greek phrase αὐτῷ διαδικάζῃ as if it were πρὸς αὐτὸν δικάζῃ.

0073.1.11.la: Colb., Reg. unus. Montef. edidit ἐπ’ αὐτοφόρῳ, facete vertens, _in via publica_ (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ τῷ φόρῳ). Sed miramur neminem perspexisse, haec, καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ ἑκάστῳ συμβήσεται, ad posteriorem, non ad priorem clausulam pertinere; reliqua vero, ἐπ’ αὐτοφ. ἐλέγξει αὐτὸν, non Symmacho, sed scholiastae deberi. Olympiodorus: Σύμμαχος γὰρ ἐκδοὺς, ἀπείη — ἀδικία (v. 10), τοῦτό φησι· μὴ εἴποιμι τὸν θεὸν ἀκρίτως τι ποιεῖν· κατὰ γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ ἑκάστῳ συμβήσεται, καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτοφόρῳ (sic) ἐλέγξει αὐτόν. E quibus verbis si quis colligat, etiam haec, καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν — συμβήσεται, Symmacho abjudicanda esse, nos quidem non vehementer repugnabimus. Hieron. vertit: _Quia reddit homini_ ※ _opus suum, et juxta viam suam unusquisque reperiet_ :.
0073.1.11.en: Colb., one Reg. Montef. edited ἐπ’ αὐτοφόρῳ, wittily rendering it _on the public road_ (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ τῷ φόρῳ). But we are surprised that no one has perceived that the words καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ ἑκάστῳ συμβήσεται belong to the latter, not to the former clause; and that the rest, ἐπ’ αὐτοφ. ἐλέγξει αὐτὸν, is due not to Symmachus but to a scholiast. Olympiodorus: Σύμμαχος γὰρ ἐκδοὺς, ἀπείη — ἀδικία (v. 10), τοῦτό φησι· μὴ εἴποιμι τὸν θεὸν ἀκρίτως τι ποιεῖν· κατὰ γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ ἑκάστῳ συμβήσεται, καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτοφόρῳ (sic) ἐλέγξει αὐτόν. If anyone should infer from these words that the words καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν — συμβήσεται too are to be denied to Symmachus, we for our part shall not strongly object. Hieron. renders: “_For he renders to man_ ※ _his work, and according to his own way each shall find_ :.”

0074.0.15.la: Colb. et Cod. 255 notant: Ἐξ Ἀκύλα καὶ Θ. τὸ ἥμισυ καὶ ὁ ἑξῆς. Hieron.: _Neque erit locus,_ ※ _et non est umbra mortis: ut latitent qui faciunt iniqua._ Syro-hex. in textu: οὐδὲ ἔστι τόπος τοῦ κρυβῆναι κ.τ.ἑ.; in marg. autem: Ἀ. Θ. οὐδὲ ἔστι σκιὰ θανάτου. Obscure Montef.: "Notat autem Colbertinus, in textu hodierno, qualem repraesentat ille, non haberi plenam lectionem, ut ab Aq. et Theod. restituta fuerat. Nam legitur ibi, οὐδὲ ἔστι (vel ἔσται) τόπος, cum certum sit Aquilam et Theod. legisse, οὐδὲ ἔστι σκιὰ θανάτου." Parsonsius e Codd. 137, 138, 139, 255, 256, scholium affert: οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ καθ᾽ ἓν (ἕνα Cod. 255) ὄψεται τὸ (τὸν Codd. 137, 139) δίκαιον.
0074.0.15.en: Colb. and Cod. 255 note: Ἐξ Ἀκύλα καὶ Θ. τὸ ἥμισυ καὶ ὁ ἑξῆς. Hieron.: "_Nor will there be a place,_ ※ _and there is no shadow of death: that those who do iniquity may hide._" Syro-hex. in the text: οὐδὲ ἔστι τόπος τοῦ κρυβῆναι κ.τ.ἑ.; but in the margin: Ἀ. Θ. οὐδὲ ἔστι σκιὰ θανάτου. Obscurely Montef.: "The Colbertine notes that in the present text, such as it represents, the full reading as it had been restored by Aq. and Theod. is not found. For there is read οὐδὲ ἔστι (or ἔσται) τόπος, whereas it is certain that Aquila and Theod. read οὐδὲ ἔστι σκιὰ θανάτου." Parsons cites from Codd. 137, 138, 139, 255, 256 a scholium: οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ καθ᾽ ἓν (ἕνα Cod. 255) ὄψεται τὸ (τὸν Codd. 137, 139) δίκαιον.

0074.0.19.la: Montef. juxta Colb. et Hieron. vv. 25–34, ab ὁ γνωρίζων ad μου τὸ ῥῆμα, quasi ex Theodotione in versionem LXXviralem inductos, siglo ※ Θ. notat. We have followed the Syrian, who gives vv. 26, 27 without asterisk; which will seem more probable to anyone comparing the Greek with the Hebrew.

Etiam sic vacant Hebraea, מַה־יִּסְכָּן־לָךְ, nisi in uno Cod. 249, qui affert: ἢ ἐρεῖς, τί κατευθύνει σοι; ἢ τί π. ἁ. Syro-hex. in marg. supplet: ܡܢܐ ܡܥܕܪ ܠܟ܀. Hieron., marks with asterisks the single lines from δυνατὸς ἰσχύϊ to ἐν εὐπρεπείαις (v. 11). But the difference of style clearly shows that the Syrian is here the best guide.

Job 37:1#0 Θ..unitText: Ο΄. Vacabat. ※ Θ. καὶ ἀπὸ ταύτης—θαυμάσια.^1

variants.en: The trembling heart and God’s wondrous thunder are added.

0078.1.1.la: "Hi undecim versiculi, utpote ex Theod. desumta, asteriscis notantur in Colb., itemque in Ed. Lat. Hieron."—_Montef._ Eosdem Theodotioni continuat Syrus noster, exceptis Graecis, καὶ ἀπερρύη ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς (v. 1), quae extra asteriscos jacent, fortasse recte. Hieronymus nescio annon Symmachi versionem ante oculos habuerit.
0078.1.1.en: "These eleven lines, as taken from Theod., are marked with asterisks in Colb., and likewise in Ed. Lat. Hieron."—_Montef._ Our Syrian continues the same for Theodotion, except the Greek words καὶ ἀπερρύη ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς (v. 1), which lie outside the asterisks, perhaps rightly. I do not know whether Hieronymus may have had the version of Symmachus before his eyes.

0079.0.16.en: Colb.: Ἐκ Θ. οἱ β΄. Montef. places the asterisk after ὑετὸς, against Syro-hex. and Hieron.

Job 37:9#0 Ἀ..unitText: Ο΄. ὀδύναι. Ἀ. συσσεισμός. Σ. Θ. καταιγίς.^20

variants.n: „Erschütterung“ statt „Schmerzen“.
variants.en: “Shaking” rather than “pains.”

0079.0.20.la: "Ἀ. συσσεισμοί. Sic Drusius [Nobil.]. At Colb. et Reg. unus habent συγκλεισμός. Iidem vero codices adjiciunt: Σ. Θ. καταιγίς."—_Montef._ Monente Schleusnero scripsimus συσσεισμός. Vocabula συγκλεισμὸς et συσσεισμὸς permutantur 2 Reg. v. 24, ubi vid. Scharfenberg. Hic quidem συγκλεισμὸς, si genuinum est, ad קָרָה, _frigus_, pertinere videtur, ad quod vocab. Olympiodorus tam καταιγὶς quam συγκλεισμὸς refert. Ejus verba sunt: Ἤτοι γὰρ τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι αἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ ψύχους ὀδύναι, ὡς ἐκ θησαυρῶν τινων, ἐξ ἀποκρύφων ἐπέρχονται· ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν περάτων καὶ τῶν ἄκρων, ὁ συγκλεισμὸς, καὶ ἡ καταιγὶς, κατὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς, ἔπεισιν.
0079.0.20.en: "Ἀ. συσσεισμοί. Thus Drusius [Nobil.]. But Colb. and one Reg. have συγκλεισμός. The same MSS. however add: Σ. Θ. καταιγίς."—_Montef._ On Schleusner's advice we have written συσσεισμός. The words συγκλεισμὸς and συσσεισμὸς are interchanged 2 Reg. v. 24, where see Scharfenberg. Here indeed συγκλεισμὸς, if genuine, seems to belong to קָרָה, _cold_, to which word Olympiodorus refers both καταιγὶς and συγκλεισμὸς. His words are: Ἤτοι γὰρ τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι αἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ ψύχους ὀδύναι, ὡς ἐκ θησαυρῶν τινων, ἐξ ἀποκρύφων ἐπέρχονται· ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν περάτων καὶ τῶν ἄκρων, ὁ συγκλεισμὸς, καὶ ἡ καταιγὶς, κατὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς, ἔπεισιν.

His words are: Ἤτοι γὰρ τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι αἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ ψύχους ὀδύναι, ὡς ἐκ θησαυρῶν τινων, ἐξ ἀποκρύφων ἐπέρχονται· ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν περάτων καὶ τῶν ἄκρων, ὁ συγκλεισμὸς, καὶ ἡ καταιγὶς, κατὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς, ἔπεισιν.

Job 38:30#0 Ὁ Ἑβραῖος.unitText: Ο΄. πρόσωπον ἀσεβοῦς τίς ἔπτηξε; Ὁ Ἑβραῖος· πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου πήγνυται.^31

variants.n: Die Oberfläche des Abgrunds gefriert statt des erschrockenen Gesichts eines Frevlers.
variants.en: The surface of the abyss freezes rather than a wicked person’s frightened face.

0083.0.31.la: "Nonnulli libri habent, τίς ἔτηξεν. [Sic Comp., Ald., Cod. Alex., alii. Syro-hex. ܡܢܘ ܦܫܪ[?]. Hieron.: _quis tabefecit._] Schol. Ὁ Ἑβραῖος· πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου πήγνυται; unde aliqua Ed. [Comp.] habet: πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου τίς ἔτηξεν. Sed magis Hebraeo responderet, si τίς ἔπηξεν legeretur."—_Nobil._ Ex sola Nobilii conjectura, ut videtur, Montef. edidit: Ἄλλος· πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου τίς ἔπηξεν;
0083.0.31.en: "Some books have τίς ἔτηξεν. [Thus Comp., Ald., Cod. Alex., and others. Syro-hex. ܡܢܘ ܦܫܪ[?]. Hieron.: _who melted._] Schol. Ὁ Ἑβραῖος· πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου πήγνυται; whence some Ed. [Comp.] has: πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου τίς ἔτηξεν. But it would correspond better to the Hebrew if τίς ἔπηξεν were read."—_Nobil._ From Nobilius' conjecture alone, as it seems, Montef. edited: Ἄλλος· πρόσωπον δὲ ἀβύσσου τίς ἔπηξεν;

0084.0.45.la: Syro-hex. in continuatione: ܡܐ ܕܡܬܐܫܕ ܥܦܪܐ ܒܬܘܫܕܐ ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ ܀ Middeld. tentat: ὅταν ἐκχύεται γῆ καταχύσει, καὶ . . . καταλαμβάνονται; (quasi scriptum esset ܡܬܕܪ̈ܟܝܢ[?], cujus tamen formae exemplum non habeo.) Pro ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ legendum videtur ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ. Tum Syriaca ad verbum sonant: καὶ θυγατέρες χειρὸς κολληθήσονται; quae quomodo cum Hebraeis concilianda sint, non video.—Haec prius scripseram quam mihi in manus venerint literae A. Ceriani, quas nunc cum lectore communicabo. “Codex: ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ ܀, superscripto scholio charactere medio inter Estranghelum et Maroniticum: ܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܐܝܠܝܢ[?]. ܡܐܩܠܐ ܕܡܢ ܩܒܠ[?] ܐܝܕܐ ܀. Locutio ܒܪ ܐܝܕܐ Nostro est ἐγχειρίδιον Jerem. l. 42. Epist. Jerem. 15; sed ipse noscis quam lata sit significatio hujus Syri idiomatis.” Hujus scholii ope, incidi in vocabulum Aquilae, Homericarum formarum imitatori, bene notum, χερμὰς s. χερμάδιον, ita dictum secundum Grammaticos, _quia manum tenentis implet._ Sic Zonaras: Χερμάδιον, ὁ χειροπλήθης λίθος, παρὰ τὸ τὴν χεῖρα πληροῦν. Conjecturam meam certo certiorem facit ipsius Aquilae usus, qui ad Deut. xxi. 21 pro Hebr. רְגָמֻהוּ[?], Ο΄. λιθοβολήσουσιν, teste Holmesii Cod. 108, χερμαδιοῦσιν interpretatus est.
0084.0.45.en: Syro-hex. in continuation: ܡܐ ܕܡܬܐܫܕ ܥܦܪܐ ܒܬܘܫܕܐ ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ ܀ Middeld. attempts: ὅταν ἐκχύεται γῆ καταχύσει, καὶ . . . καταλαμβάνονται; (as if ܡܬܕܪ̈ܟܝܢ[?] were written, of which form, however, I have no example.) For ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ it seems we should read ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ. Then the Syriac means word for word: καὶ θυγατέρες χειρὸς κολληθήσονται; how this is to be reconciled with the Hebrew I do not see.—I had written this before the letter of A. Ceriani came into my hands, which I shall now share with the reader. “The MS.: ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ ܀, with a scholium written above in a script intermediate between Estrangela and Maronite: ܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܐܝܠܝܢ[?]. ܡܐܩܠܐ ܕܡܢ ܩܒܠ[?] ܐܝܕܐ ܀. The phrase ܒܪ ܐܝܕܐ is in our translator ἐγχειρίδιον Jerem. l. 42. Epist. Jerem. 15; but you yourself know how wide the meaning of this Syriac idiom is.” With the help of this scholium I hit upon a word well known to Aquila, an imitator of Homeric forms, χερμὰς or χερμάδιον, so called according to the Grammarians _because it fills the hand of the one holding it._ Thus Zonaras: Χερμάδιον, ὁ χειροπλήθης λίθος, παρὰ τὸ τὴν χεῖρα πληροῦν. My conjecture is made more than certain by Aquila's own usage, who at Deut. xxi. 21 for the Hebrew רְגָמֻהוּ[?], Ο΄. λιθοβολήσουσιν, rendered χερμαδιοῦσιν, on the testimony of Holmes' Cod. 108.

0084.0.46.la: Syro-hex. Symmacho continuat: ܐܡܬܝ ܕܐܫܬܦܟ ܒܥܦܪܐ ܕܐܪܥܐ ܐܫܬܦܟܘܬܐ ܐܝܟܢܐ ܕܩܠ̈ܩܠܐ ܢܗܘܘܢ ܒܢܩܦܘܬܐ ܕܐܟܚܕܐ[?] ܀ Hic venit in auxilium Cod. 252: Ἀ. γῆς ἐπίχυσις ἵνα βῶλοι γένωνται συγκολληθεῖσαι; quae manifesto non Aquilae, sed Symmacho vindicanda sunt.

Conjecturam meam certo certiorem facit ipsius Aquilae usus, qui ad Deut. xxi. 21 pro Hebr. רְגָמֻהוּ[?], Ο΄. λιθοβολήσουσιν, teste Holmesii Cod. 108, χερμαδιοῦσιν interpretatus est.
0084.0.45.en: Syro-hex. in continuation: ܡܐ ܕܡܬܐܫܕ ܥܦܪܐ ܒܬܘܫܕܐ ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ ܀ Middeld. attempts: ὅταν ἐκχύεται γῆ καταχύσει, καὶ . . . καταλαμβάνονται; (as if ܡܬܕܪ̈ܟܝܢ[?] were written, of which form, however, I have no example.) For ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܝܢ it seems we should read ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ. Then the Syriac means word for word: καὶ θυγατέρες χειρὸς κολληθήσονται; how this is to be reconciled with the Hebrew I do not see.—I had written this before the letter of A. Ceriani came into my hands, which I shall now share with the reader. “The MS.: ܘܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܡܬܢܩ̈ܦܢ ܀, with a scholium written above in a script intermediate between Estrangela and Maronite: ܒܢ̈ܬ ܐܝܕܐ ܐܝܠܝܢ[?]. ܡܐܩܠܐ ܕܡܢ ܩܒܠ[?] ܐܝܕܐ ܀. The phrase ܒܪ ܐܝܕܐ is in our translator ἐγχειρίδιον Jerem. l. 42. Epist. Jerem. 15; but you yourself know how wide the meaning of this Syriac idiom is.” With the help of this scholium I hit upon a word well known to Aquila, an imitator of Homeric forms, χερμὰς or χερμάδιον, so called according to the Grammarians _because it fills the hand of the one holding it._ Thus Zonaras: Χερμάδιον, ὁ χειροπλήθης λίθος, παρὰ τὸ τὴν χεῖρα πληροῦν. My conjecture is made more than certain by Aquila's own usage, who at Deut. xxi. 21 for the Hebrew רְגָמֻהוּ[?], Ο΄. λιθοβολήσουσιν, rendered χερμαδιοῦσιν, on the testimony of Holmes' Cod. 108.

0086.0.39.la: Syrus affert: ܬ. ※ ܒܙܘܥܐ ܕܪܘܡܬܐ[?] ܘܕܡܓܢܐ[?] ܀. Deinde notat: “Non positum erat apud Origenem.” Pro ܕܪܘܡܬܐ[?] Kreyssigius ingeniose conjecit ܕܪܘܡܚܐ, et sic reapse codex. Eodem pertinere videtur Cod. 249, qui post μάχαιραν addit: λόγχη (sic) καὶ ἀσπίδος σεισμός. Propter rationes autem grammaticas ordinem verborum mutavit Syrus. Totum v. sic vertit Hieron.: _Super ipsum autem gaudet arcus et gladius,_ ※ _lanceae hastaeque tremore._
0086.0.39.en: The Syrian cites: ܬ. ※ ܒܙܘܥܐ ܕܪܘܡܬܐ[?] ܘܕܡܓܢܐ[?] ܀. Then he notes: “It was not placed in Origen.” For ܕܪܘܡܬܐ[?] Kreyssig ingeniously conjectured ܕܪܘܡܚܐ, and so in fact the MS. To the same seems to belong Cod. 249, which after μάχαιραν adds: λόγχη (sic) καὶ ἀσπίδος σεισμός. For grammatical reasons, however, the Syrian changed the order of the words. Hieron. renders the whole verse thus: “_But over him the bow and the sword rejoice,_ ※ _with the quivering of lance and spear._”

0087.1.2.la: Montef. pro Hebraeis וְאִם־זְרוֹעַ כָּאֵל לָךְ ex Colb., Reg. affert: Σ. ἀκυρώσεις . . . ὡς θεοῦ ὑπάρχῃς. Vocab. ἀκυρώσεις ad v. 3 pertinere videtur: pro ὑπάρχῃς autem fortasse legendum ὑπάρχει σοι. Syrus noster in textu pro κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου habet ὡς θεοῦ (ܐܝܟ ܕܐܠܗܐ), apposito in marg. ܡܪܝܐ (ܐܝܟ), κατὰ κύριον, ut Codd. III, 23.

The word ἀκυρώσεις seems to belong to v. 3; for ὑπάρχῃς, however, perhaps ὑπάρχει σοι should be read. Our Syrian in the text for κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου has ὡς θεοῦ (ܐܝܟ ܕܐܠܗܐ), with ܡܪܝܐ (ܐܝܟ), κατὰ κύριον, placed in the margin, as Codd. III, 23.

0087.1.5.la: Montef. ad Hebr. הַכְנִיעֵהוּ, _deprime eum_, affert: Ἀ. καὶ ἀπόρριψον (ἄλλ. ἐπίστρεψον), notans: “Ἀ. ἀπόρριψον. Colb. et Reg. unus. Apud Drusium legitur ἐπίστρεψον.” Nobil., quem imitatus est Drusius, ad σῆψον δὲ affert: Ἀ. ἐπίστρεψον, et sic, teste Parsonsio, Cod. 248. Sed idem Parsons. ad κρύψον δὲ (v. 8) exscripsit: Ἀ. καὶ ἐπίρριψον. Cod. 138. Σ. καὶ ἐπίρριψον. Codd. 137, 139; ubi in Hebr. est טָמְנֵם, _absconde eos._ In re incerta mediam lectionem, καὶ ἐπίρριψον, probavimus, et Hebraeo וַהֲדֹךְ propter copulam aptavimus.
0087.1.5.en: Montef. on the Hebrew הַכְנִיעֵהוּ, _bring him low_, cites: Ἀ. καὶ ἀπόρριψον (ἄλλ. ἐπίστρεψον), noting: “Ἀ. ἀπόρριψον. Colb. and one Reg. In Drusius ἐπίστρεψον is read.” Nobil., whom Drusius imitated, cites on σῆψον δὲ: Ἀ. ἐπίστρεψον, and so, on Parsons' testimony, Cod. 248. But the same Parsons on κρύψον δὲ (v. 8) transcribed: Ἀ. καὶ ἐπίρριψον. Cod. 138. Σ. καὶ ἐπίρριψον. Codd. 137, 139; where in the Hebrew there is טָמְנֵם, _hide them._ In an uncertain matter we have approved the middle reading, καὶ ἐπίρριψον, and fitted it to the Hebrew וַהֲדֹךְ on account of the copula.

0088.0.20.la: Lectio ἄγνου, _viticis_, est in Comp., Ald., Cod. Alex., aliis. Syrus noster habet ܕܫܘܚܠܦܐ, apposito in marg. ΑΓΝΟΥ. Middeld. in _Curis Hex._ ad loc.: “ܫܘܚܠܦܐ in Lexico redditur _variatio, mutatio_ [cf. Hex. nostra ad Ezech. xlv. 11]; sed perspicuum idem esse quod ܫܚܠܦܐ[?], _germen, surculus._” Conferenda sunt vocabula Chald. חִלְפָא, _juncus_, et הִילְפָא, _salix._
0088.0.20.en: The reading ἄγνου, _of the chaste-tree_, is in Comp., Ald., Cod. Alex., and others. Our Syrian has ܕܫܘܚܠܦܐ, with ΑΓΝΟΥ placed in the margin. Middeld. in _Curae Hex._ on the passage: “ܫܘܚܠܦܐ is rendered in the Lexicon _variation, change_ [cf. our Hex. on Ezech. xlv. 11]; but it is clear that it is the same as ܫܚܠܦܐ[?], _shoot, sprout._” The Chaldee words חִלְפָא, _rush_, and הִילְפָא, _willow_, are to be compared.

0091.0.33.la: “Hic versiculus, qui in LXX legitur, ex Ἀ. Θ. cum asterisco notatur in Colbertino.”—_Montef._ Neque Syro-hex., neque Hieron. asteriscum agnoscit. Ed. Rom. legit σφυρὰ (sic): sed Colb. et Syro-hex. cum Comp., Ald. et codd. σφῦραι tuentur.
0091.0.33.en: “This line, which is read in the LXX, is marked with an asterisk as from Ἀ. Θ. in the Colbertine.”—_Montef._ Neither Syro-hex. nor Hieron. recognizes the asterisk. Ed. Rom. reads σφυρὰ (sic): but Colb. and Syro-hex., with Comp., Ald. and the MSS., support σφῦραι.

0091.0.34.la: Syro-hex. ܣ. ܐܝܟ ܩܫܐ[?] ܚܫܝܒ ܠܗ ܐܪܙܦܬܐ ܀. (Juxta Syri interpretis usum ܐܬܚܫܒ sonaret ἐλογίσθη, et ܚܫܝܒ λελόγισται s. ἥγηται, quod posterius vocab. pro passivo perperam cepit idem vv. 20, 21, 23. Sed non crediderim Symmachum soloecum ἥγηται αὐτῷ scripsisse; altera autem versio ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ σφῦρα in Codd. III, 23 reperitur.)
0091.0.34.en: Syro-hex. ܣ. ܐܝܟ ܩܫܐ[?] ܚܫܝܒ ܠܗ ܐܪܙܦܬܐ ܀. (According to the usage of the Syrian translator ܐܬܚܫܒ would mean ἐλογίσθη, and ܚܫܝܒ λελόγισται or ἥγηται, which latter word the same translator wrongly took as passive in vv. 20, 21, 23. But I would not believe that Symmachus wrote the solecism ἥγηται αὐτῷ; the other version, ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ σφῦρα, is found in Codd. III, 23.)

0107.0.12.la: Syro-hex. ܐ. ܣ. ܬ. ܡܢ ܙܒܢܐ ܕܪܕܝܐ ◆ Vertit Bugatus: _a tempore decursus._ Cf. nos ad Hos. ii. 22, in _Otio Norv._ p. 68. Ceterum in hac versione trium interpp., vocabulum χεῦμα ad Aquilam solum pertinere manifestum est. Tres interpp. καιροῦ pro καρποῦ vertisse testatur Vat., notans: Οἱ Γ΄ ὁμοίως, h. e. τοῖς Ο΄, qui, teste Origene (Opp. T. II, p. 574) ἀπὸ καιροῦ posuerunt. Syro-hex. tamen in textu habet, ἀπὸ καρποῦ.
0107.0.12.en: Syro-hex. ܐ. ܣ. ܬ. ܡܢ ܙܒܢܐ ܕܪܕܝܐ ◆ Bugati renders: _from the time of the flowing._ Cf. our note on Hos. ii. 22, in _Otium Norv._ p. 68. For the rest, in this version of the three translators it is manifest that the word χεῦμα belongs to Aquila alone. That the three translators rendered καιροῦ for καρποῦ is attested by Vat., noting: Οἱ Γ΄ ὁμοίως, i.e. τοῖς Ο΄, who, on Origen's testimony (Opp. T. II, p. 574), put ἀπὸ καιροῦ. Syro-hex., however, has in the text ἀπὸ καρποῦ.

variants.en: A garden bed prepared for water rather than a deer longing for water.

0170.1.2.la: Montef. ex Nobil. affert: Ἀ. ὡς αὐλὼν πεπρασίασται. Plenius Syro-hex.: Ἀ. ὡς αὐλὼν πεπρασιασμένος (ܐܝܟ ܐܘܠܢܐ[?] ܕܡܦܪܣܣ[?]) ἐπὶ ἐκχύσεις (ܡܦܩ̈ܐ. Vid. ad Psal. xvii. 16) ὑδάτων. A nomine עֲרוּגָה, _areola in horto_, πρασιὰ (Aq. ad Cant. Cant. v. 13. vi. 2) Aquila more suo extudit verba πρασιάζομαι, πρασιόομαι, unde πεπρασίασται h. l., et ἐπρασιώθη Joel. i. 20, quae Schleusnerus ad unicam formam πρασιάομαι imperite refert. Syrus noster pro πρασιὰ (Anglice, _bed_) ܡܦܪܣܣܬܐ[?] adhibet Cant. Cant. v. 13, ut hic pro πεπρασιασμένος, ܕܡܦܪܣܣ[?]. Montef. notat: “Hieronymus Aquilam de more secutus, αὐλὼν vertit, _areola praeparata_.” Immo Hieronymi versio est: _sicut areola praeparata ad irrigationes aquarum_; ut _praeparata_ ad πεπρασιασμένος referatur.
0170.1.2.en: Montef. cites from Nobil.: Ἀ. ὡς αὐλὼν πεπρασίασται. More fully Syro-hex.: Ἀ. ὡς αὐλὼν πεπρασιασμένος (ܐܝܟ ܐܘܠܢܐ[?] ܕܡܦܪܣܣ[?]) ἐπὶ ἐκχύσεις (ܡܦܩ̈ܐ. See on Psal. xvii. 16) ὑδάτων. From the noun עֲרוּגָה, _a bed in a garden_, πρασιὰ (Aq. on Cant. Cant. v. 13. vi. 2), Aquila after his manner hammered out the verbs πρασιάζομαι, πρασιόομαι, whence πεπρασίασται in this place, and ἐπρασιώθη Joel. i. 20, which Schleusner unskilfully refers to a single form πρασιάομαι. Our Syrian uses ܡܦܪܣܣܬܐ[?] for πρασιὰ (English _bed_) at Cant. Cant. v. 13, as here ܕܡܦܪܣܣ[?] for πεπρασιασμένος. Montef. notes: “Jerome, following Aquila as usual, renders αὐλὼν _a prepared bed_.” Rather, Jerome’s version is: _as a bed prepared for the irrigations of waters_; so that _prepared_ is to be referred to πεπρασιασμένος.

0241.0.17.la: Euseb. Nobil., Euthym.: Σ. ἐχολώθη. Syro-hex. ܣ. ܘܪܓܙ܀. Pro καὶ ἀνεβάλετο idem in textu habet, ܘܐܬܬܘܝ[?], _et distulit;_ in marg. autem: ܘܐܬܥܛܦ܀, _et amictus est_, notans: “_Distulit_, hoc est, de adjutorio eorum; _amictus est_, hoc est, accinxit seipsum adversus eos.” Priorem sensum Graecus quidam apud Agellium sic explanat: ἀντὶ τοῦ, ὑπερέθετο μικρὸν, καὶ οἱονεὶ ἀνέκοψε τὴν εὐεργετικὴν χεῖρα. Aquilam secutus est Hieron.: _et non distulit._
0241.0.17.en: Euseb. Nobil., Euthym.: Σ. ἐχολώθη. Syro-hex. ܣ. ܘܪܓܙ܀. For καὶ ἀνεβάλετο the same has in the text ܘܐܬܬܘܝ[?], _and he delayed;_ but in the margin: ܘܐܬܥܛܦ܀, _and he was clothed_, noting: “‘_He delayed_’, that is, in helping them; ‘_he was clothed_’, that is, he girded himself against them.” The former sense a certain Greek in Agellius explains thus: ἀντὶ τοῦ, ὑπερέθετο μικρὸν, καὶ οἱονεὶ ἀνέκοψε τὴν εὐεργετικὴν χεῖρα. Hieron. followed Aquila: “_and he did not delay._”
